evidence.location: section 2, IR1, first bullet, the (p1) sentence: its includes are composed under the model's directory with the loader gnd check uses (_load_model_at under retained_root, R0.3), without binding references there
evidence.observation: The plan r3 (p1) sentence requires composing without binding references and then binding via bind_declared_references at --reference-root. The IR1 draft spec (notes/phase-IR1-spec.md, section 6 step 3, line 96: model = load_model_bytes_composed(mr, source=model_path, root=root), and the raw-subject check at line 129: loaded = load_model_bytes_composed(model_bytes, ..., root=model_root)) still names load_model_bytes_composed, which binds references under the composition root (src/gnd/model/__init__.py:371-377, model._references = _bind_at(model, descriptor)); the spec's own section 2 says it was written against plan r2. ReferenceInputError is a ValueError subclass, so under that entry point a root whose reference file lives only under --reference-root refuses at composition and plan criterion IR1-C8 fails as drafted - exactly the defect round 1 recorded as fixed by this (p1) sentence (disposition row ir1-composed-loader-ignores-reference-root, model/__init__.py:362-376).

concerns.recommendation: Rewrite the IR1 spec against r3 before its delegated gate: compose via _load_model_at under retained_root with no reference binding in both api.judgments and the evaluate_judgments raw-subject check, and have the spec gate check that the spec names no other composed entry point.
concerns.title: IR1 draft spec still binds references during composition, contradicting r3's (p1) no-binding sentence and IR1-C8

evidence.location: section 0, R0.6 (A model without includes is untouched. Every changed route gives byte-identical output for a model that declares no includes.) read with section 2 IR1 first bullet (Only a root that declares includes takes the composed route) and criterion IR1-C7 (a model without includes gives the byte-identical report it gives today)
evidence.observation: Neither R0.6 nor IR1-C7 defines a model without includes for a version-5 document carrying fact_type_constraints and no includes key. Today api.judgments refuses that document with include:unsupported-route (guard_document -> declares_includes at src/gnd/model/_includes.py:279-281, which is true for the fact_type_constraints key); after the guards are dropped its refusal code changes on either branch reading - via the composed loader (parse_declarations, _includes.py:64-66, refuses declaration because document.get('includes') is not a list) or via unrooted load_model_bytes, which representation-format.md lines 1895-1896 say refuses orphan fact_type_constraints with include:declaration - and D6 also moves error.reason to binding. So under the literal reading of declares no includes R0.6 cannot hold for this input class, and under the declares_includes() helper reading it holds only because the class counts as declaring includes, a predicate the plan never states.

concerns.recommendation: State the branch predicate and the scope explicitly in the plan or the IR1 spec: define declares includes as declares_includes() (includes or fact_type_constraints) and scope R0.6/IR1-C7 to documents declaring neither, so the orphan-attachment refusal change from include:unsupported-route to include:declaration is either acknowledged and pinned or kept out of the changed set.
concerns.title: R0.6 and IR1-C7 leave the orphan fact_type_constraints class undefined, and its refusal code changes under either reading
